name: Volza
summary: Export-import trade intelligence: search customs-level shipment records to find verified buyers and suppliers. Downloads run on a published credit allowance, from 360,000 full-shipment credits a year.
best_for: import-export businesses and sourcing teams that want global customs-level trade data plus verified buyer/supplier contacts at a fraction of enterprise pricing
skip_if: you only need US shipment data with fast daily updates (ImportGenius refreshes daily), or you're not doing import/export: this is a niche intelligence tool
honest_knock:
Three honest catches. The entry plan is narrower than the marketing implies: $1,500 a year covers 182 countries and two users, while the 200-country coverage and ten seats start at $4,500. Downloads run on a credit allowance (360,000 a year on Startup) and an earlier reading of the catalogue put the cost per record at one credit for US or India shipments and up to ten in thinner markets; that per-country rate is not stated on the current pricing page and we could not re-verify it on 1 September 2026, so treat it as a question for sales rather than a fact. And the update cycle is slow, with some datasets taking up to two months to refresh, which suits structural questions far better than reactive ones. There is a learning curve too; it rewards analysts, not casual users.

There is no monthly plan. Between the 'Annually' and '2-Year Value Plan' toggles, the smallest paid commitment is $1,500 for a year, so a buyer with one short sourcing question should get the answer out of the trial rather than out of a subscription. And the 2-year discount is real but modest in cash terms: $450 off on Startup, $1,350 on SME and $2,880 on Corporate, against two annual terms that you pay up front and cannot spread.

pricing.notes: (price re-verified 2026-11-09 on volza.com/pricing in a browser, because the page returns HTTP 403 to plain fetches; earlier reads 2026-09-01 and 2026-09-23) Three paid plans, billed annually or as a 2-Year Value Plan, and a free trial; the page shows no monthly price. Startup is $1,500 a year: 182 countries (44 export and 50 import detailed databases, plus mirror and one-side databases; the 23 September reading listed 160 export and 158 import mirror and 7 and 7 one-side, premium countries excluded), data from 2014 onward, 6,000 searches, full shipment view, 360,000 full-shipment download credits and 2 users. SME is $4,500 a year: the card now says 200+ countries (it said 200 on 23 September), adds the statistical databases (46 export, 48 import), unlimited searches under fair use, 1,040,000 download credits and 10 users. Corporate is $9,600 a year: the same 200+ country coverage, unlimited searches under fair use, 2,400,000 download credits and 15 users. The free trial now runs 3 months with no credit card (it was 7 days on 23 September), is advertised as "50$ On sign up + Unlimited Volza credits", and shows the last three years in full view with the latest six months as a preview; on 23 September it carried no full-shipment download credits and allowed 10 users, rows we did not re-check on 9 November. The 2-Year Value Plan is paid for two years at once and advertised as 15% saving plus 15% bonus credits: Startup $2,550, SME $7,650, Corporate $16,320, which is exactly two annual terms less 15%. On 23 September the 2-year cards showed 13,800 searches, 828,000 download credits and 5 users for Startup, 2,392,000 credits for SME and 5,520,000 for Corporate. The comparison table caps workspaces at 75, 300 and 600 (Startup, SME, Corporate; 'as per credits' on the trial) and shipments per workspace at 300,000 on the trial and Startup, 500,000 on SME and 750,000 on Corporate; on 23 September it also capped workspace deletions at 20, 75 and 100 a month. The page also states a refund promise: if you find no profitable opportunity, Volza will help you find one or refund in full.
